# Global Memory Index

Cross-project reference material and patterns too specific for
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` but applicable across projects.

This directory holds reference docs, technical patterns, and things
Claude greps on-demand.

## References

- [reference_immunefi_workflow.md](reference_immunefi_workflow.md) — Immunefi bug report review workflow via Brave CDP + Playwright (Magnus dashboard, Quick Action UI, scripted helpers)
- [reference_notion_cdp_workflow.md](reference_notion_cdp_workflow.md) — Generic Notion-via-Brave-CDP technical reference. Read body via `.notion-*-block` classes; comments via `.notion-page-view-discussion`. Includes anti-patterns and row-contamination gotchas. Read BEFORE editing any Notion doc via CDP.
- [reference_playwright_web_automation.md](reference_playwright_web_automation.md) — Playwright API for web automation: connect to existing browser via CDP, fill forms, click buttons, screenshots
- [reference_scripts_storage.md](reference_scripts_storage.md) — Where to put session-created scripts. Persistent helpers live in `~/.claude/scripts/<category>/` (synced via Syncthing, symlinked from every profile); ephemeral probes stay in `/tmp/`. Affects API calls only (commits + push use git config + SSH which are unaffected). Fix: `eval "$(direnv export bash)" && gh ...` or `direnv exec . gh ...`. Promoted from subspace/core-v1/hub-modules on 2026-05-21.

- [feedback_app_namespace_convention.md](feedback_app_namespace_convention.md) — Reverse-DNS namespace for LaunchDaemon plists / app bundle ids defaults to `dev.<redacted-user>.<app>` (personal domain). Project-specific (com.subspace, com.granite, etc.) only when the work is specifically for that project.
- [feedback_test_dont_delegate.md](feedback_test_dont_delegate.md) — When asked to test/verify a change, drive the test yourself via available tools (MCP, logs, bash) — never hand the user a manual checklist for behaviors you can verify programmatically
- [feedback_test_regression_restart.md](feedback_test_regression_restart.md) — When a regression / fix lands mid-test-sequence, restart the entire test sequence from Test 1 (not where we stopped) — re-confirms the whole chain under the fresh binary
- [feedback_pr_review_fold_in_rubric.md](feedback_pr_review_fold_in_rubric.md) — When reviewing PRs, decide whether non-blocking observations fold into THIS PR or defer to a follow-up. - [feedback_pr_review_canonical_case_check.md](feedback_pr_review_canonical_case_check.md) — When a PR touches filesystem layout, cross-process state, or "where do files actually live" assumptions, the reviewer MUST verify on-disk against the canonical real-world layout. CI mocks bypass directory-filter logic; mocked-fixture tests can't catch layout assumptions.

Cross-session memory loss + in-flight work means stored routing state can be stale. One shell call avoids wasted worker cycles.

- [feedback_v1_scope_expansion_load_bearing.md](feedback_v1_scope_expansion_load_bearing.md) — If shipping v1 without an item leaves the user-visible promise hollow, fold the v2 item into v1. "V2" is a planning placeholder, not a correctness guarantee.
- [feedback_planner_commit_with_reasoning.md](feedback_planner_commit_with_reasoning.md) — Planner/coordinator default: commit to a recommendation with stated reasoning. Lead sees the reasoning + can override fast. Escalate only for genuine uncertainty, beyond-authority calls, or high-reversibility-cost decisions.

- [brief_intellij_review_pipeline_2026_04_22.md](brief_intellij_review_pipeline_2026_04_22.md) — user-scope review pipeline for IntelliJ projects. Handoff from forge parity-complete milestone into pipeline-design session. Read before designing; don't start coding until brainstorm done.
- [brief_chain_indexer_pool_collapse_2026_05_08.md](brief_chain_indexer_pool_collapse_2026_05_08.md) — `Subspace::new_from_url` in autonomys/subspace-chain-alerts (`shared/src/subspace.rs`) blocks indefinitely when the substrate RPC is unreachable at startup, because the underlying `ReconnectingRpcClient::build` retries with infinite exponential backoff. Self-contained binary using `hudsucker` + `rcgen` for auto-generated CA, wrapper mode that spawns child with env vars set, defensive scanning for drift detection. Includes full Cargo.toml, src/main.rs (~350 lines), drift_check.rs sketch, 10 known gotchas, success criteria. # Cross-Project TIL Index

Today-I-Learned entries — cross-project patterns, workarounds, and
insights worth remembering beyond the project they were learned in.

Newest first. Each entry is a separate file; this is the index.

<!-- TIL entries will appear below this line -->

- [2026-05-27-macos-usb-device-userclient-grab.md](2026-05-27-macos-usb-device-userclient-grab.md) — 2026-05-27: USB camera/mic "physically connected but invisible to macOS" — `SPCameraDataType`/`SPAudioDataType` empty, `AVCaptureDevice` doesn't list it, even though `ioreg` shows the device matched at IOUSBHostDevice level. Cause: an Electron/CEF app or Brave Browser called WebUSB / IOUSBLib and **exclusively claimed the device via `AppleUSBHostDeviceUserClient`**, which blocks `AppleUSBHostCompositeDevice` (`!registered, !matched` in ioreg) from splitting the device into camera + audio interfaces. UVCAssistant / AppleUSBAudio class drivers can't attach. Observed holders: IntelliJ IDEA's `cef_server` helper holding a Logitech C920; Brave tabs with WebUSB usage. Detection: `ioreg -l -w 0 | grep -A 50 "<device product name>"` → look for `IOUserClientCreator = pid X, <process>` and `AppleUSBHostCompositeDevice ... !matched`. Fix: kill the holder PID (`kill -9 <pid>`; for Brave `pkill -9 -f "Brave Browser"`), then **physically unplug + replug the USB cable** — macOS does NOT auto-re-probe a USB device after a userclient releases; composite driver only matches on fresh enumeration. After replug, `UVCAssistant` claims cleanly and the device shows up everywhere. Generalises to any USB camera/mic/MIDI/HID device that suddenly goes invisible on macOS; macOS-specific (Linux/Windows handle userclient cleanup differently).
- [2026-05-21-macos-26-trust-settings-admin-write-locked.md](2026-05-21-macos-26-trust-settings-admin-write-locked.md) - 2026-05-21: macOS 26 Tahoe hardened `com.apple.trust-settings.admin` against authorizationdb writes - returns `NO (-60005)` errSecParam on every form (`allow` arg, plist on stdin, even verbatim round-trip). The classic sysadmin trick of temporarily relaxing the right to silence SecurityAgent during unattended cert installs no longer works. `security add-trusted-cert -d` to admin trust domain now ALWAYS prompts Touch ID via SecurityAgent, independent of sudo NOPASSWD. Silent-failure mode in headless contexts (sudo -n exits 0, cert never lands). Workaround: content-idempotent install via SHA-256 fingerprint compare - skip the add entirely unless disk CA differs from keychain copy. **Companion gotcha:** `security find-certificate -c <name>` matches CN ONLY, not the whole subject DN - so `-c "<organisation>"` finds nothing even when the cert is present (forge CA has CN="forge wire-classification rewriter", O="forge-tui"; matching by O silently fails). Always `openssl x509 -in <pem> -noout -subject` before hard-coding a `-c` value; or use `-Z <sha1>` for unambiguous identity. Generalises to any unattended cert install pattern that was working on earlier macOS via authorizationdb override.
- [2026-05-06-no-claude-attribution-leakage-in-commits.md](2026-05-06-no-claude-attribution-leakage-in-commits.md) - 2026-05-06: The harness ships a default commit-message HEREDOC ending in `Co-Authored-By: Claude` and a "Generated with..." footer, plus the system prompt strongly nudges that template. The user's CLAUDE.md flips this to "never reveal Claude/AI involvement in third-party-visible artifacts" - co-author trailers, "Generated with" footers, "review loop" / round-N / agent-role-name phrasing all banned. The user's rule wins (CLAUDE.md overrides defaults), but the default's strength means it can still leak through. Counter-pattern: actively prune the default suffix from every commit before sending; treat any LLM-tell phrasing in a public commit as a bug.
- [emby-datecreated-sticky-to-path.md](emby-datecreated-sticky-to-path.md) — 2026-05-18: Emby's `DateCreated` is pinned to the (item, path) tuple, NOT the file content — same-path file replacements (common when Radarr/Sonarr's quality-tag heuristic produces identical filenames for old + new release, e.g. PreDVD mis-tagged as `WEBDL-1080p` then upgraded to a real WEBDL-1080p at the same path) leave DateCreated untouched and the item never surfaces in "Recently Added". `MinDateLastSaved` is the opposite failure — too noisy, triggers on any metadata refresh. The only reliable signal is file mtime on disk: `:ro` bind-mount the media root at the same path Emby uses (`/mnt/movies/...`), stat `MediaSources[0].Path` mtime client-side, compare to a persisted last-run cursor. Bit hub-modules PR #104 silently for days — auto-unmark task reported 0 items every 30-min run while ~13 real upgrades went unmarked. Same shape almost certainly applies to Jellyfin (Emby fork) and Plex (`addedAt` is item-creation, `updatedAt` is metadata refresh). Generalises: for content-replacement detection, the filesystem is the only authoritative source — media-server metadata DBs track intents and refreshes, not bytes.
- [2026-05-17-spotlight-indexes-cargo-target.md](2026-05-17-spotlight-indexes-cargo-target.md) — 2026-05-17: macOS Spotlight indexes cargo `target/` by default. Every build writes hundreds of fresh files (`.fingerprint/`, `incremental/`, hash-suffixed binaries) → `mds_worker` / `corespotlightd` queue all of them → file-handle contention with subsequent build steps. Bites hardest right after a source change. Symptom: cargo-nextest PID at 0.07s CPU for 20+ minutes with empty stdout, rustc child processes flickering in and out. Diagnose with `mdfind -onlyin <repo>/target "kMDItemKind == 'Unix Executable File'"` — hits mean Spotlight is indexing. Fix: drop a `.metadata_never_index` sentinel file in each `target/` (Apple-documented since 10.4, still respected on macOS 26): `find ~/Projects -name target -type d -maxdepth 4 -exec touch {}/.metadata_never_index \;` (plus a sibling-`Cargo.toml` check to avoid non-cargo target/ dirs). Pairs with the XProtect Developer Tools fix from earlier today — XProtect = per-binary exec scan, Spotlight = per-file write index. Both layers needed for sub-10s test cycles. Same payload across accounts → genuine local cache. Different payload → account-scoped, working as designed. Applies to any auth-API wrapper (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Slack, AWS, etc.).
- [2026-05-04-sonarr-tvsearch-indexer-side-parsing.md](2026-05-04-sonarr-tvsearch-indexer-side-parsing.md) — 2026-05-04 (workarounds corrected 2026-05-06): Sonarr's tvsearch hits per-app endpoints with `&season=N&ep=M` filters; indexers run their OWN parser to TV-tag releases, and titles like `2026x29` (vs `S2026E29`) fail that pre-parse — invisible to tvsearch despite high seeders. Bypass at qBittorrent level: Prowlarr generic search → grab `magnetUrl` → POST to qBit's `/api/v2/torrents/add` with `category=<sonarr-tv>` + `savepath=/downloads`. Sonarr's downloads handler imports based on filename parsing (must match TVDB's episode numbering — Sprint releases using `2026x37` for E27 fail this and need manual-import). - [2026-05-03-sqlite-fk-toggle-table-rebuild.md](2026-05-03-sqlite-fk-toggle-table-rebuild.md) — 2026-05-03: SQLite can't `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT`; rebuild via CREATE NEW → INSERT → DROP OLD → RENAME. Backfill non-conforming rows BEFORE rebuild so the new CHECK accepts everything.

Never fall back to user/global-scope token as a "close enough" alternative — that may also be the wrong account. Near-miss: tried to use `granite-backend`'s `hackercf` token to cut a `<redacted-user>/claude-code-proxy` release. Three-part pattern: `setopt LOCAL_OPTIONS NO_MONITOR NO_NOTIFY` at function top silences zsh's `[N] PID / [N] Done` job-control noise; spawn `(slow > $tmp) &` + `wait $pid`; rewrite with `\033[nA\r\033[K<line>\033[nB\r` (up n, col 0, clear, reprint, down n). Example: `ws wg status` egress field in dotfiles ws.zsh.
- [2026-04-23-nix-darwin-launchdaemon-nix-store-boot-race.md](2026-04-23-nix-darwin-launchdaemon-nix-store-boot-race.md) — 2026-04-23: On macOS with Determinate Nix, a `launchd.daemons.*` plist whose `ProgramArguments[0]` is a `/nix/store/.../bin/foo` path silently fails to auto-load at boot — launchd scans `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` before `/nix/store` is synthesized via firmlink, no log entry, daemon just skipped. Fix: entrypoint must live on `/` — use `/bin/bash -c` with a 60s polling wait for `/run/current-system/sw/bin/<tool>` then `exec`. Matches the pattern already used by in-repo nix-darwin LaunchAgents.
- [2026-04-22-intellij-mcp-sse-port-plus-1000.md](2026-04-22-intellij-mcp-sse-port-plus-1000.md) — 2026-04-22: IntelliJ 2026.1's MCP Server plugin dropped the legacy `/api/mcp/list_tools` paths that `@jetbrains/mcp-proxy` (the official stdio shim) still polls — it now speaks standard MCP SSE on builtin-webserver-port + 1000 (63342 → 64342) at `/sse`. - [2026-04-22-intellij-bundledkeymap-bare-filename.md](2026-04-22-intellij-bundledkeymap-bare-filename.md) — 2026-04-22: IntelliJ `<bundledKeymap file="X.xml" />` must use a BARE filename (no `/keymaps/` path prefix). - [2026-04-22-resilience-patterns-for-any-codebase.md](2026-04-22-resilience-patterns-for-any-codebase.md) — 2026-04-22: Portable checklist of resilience/performance patterns that apply to any backend/service/agent codebase — retry with backoff, batch DB writes, idempotency via unique index + ON CONFLICT, rate limiting, timeouts, context propagation, singleflight, cache invalidation on rejection, per-item failure aggregation, cost-of-scale math before shipping. # Ralph Wiggum Plugin Help

Please explain the following to the user:

## What is the Ralph Wiggum Technique?

The Ralph Wiggum technique is an iterative development methodology based on continuous AI loops, pioneered by Geoffrey Huntley.

**Core concept:**
```bash
while :; do
  cat PROMPT.md | claude-code --continue
done
```

The same prompt is fed to Claude repeatedly. The "self-referential" aspect comes from Claude seeing its own previous work in the files and git history, not from feeding output back as input.

**Each iteration:**
1. Claude receives the SAME prompt
2. Works on the task, modifying files
3. Tries to exit
4. Stop hook intercepts and feeds the same prompt again
5. Claude sees its previous work in the files
6. Iteratively improves until completion

The technique is described as "deterministically bad in an undeterministic world" - failures are predictable, enabling systematic improvement through prompt tuning.

## Available Commands

### /ralph-loop <PROMPT> [OPTIONS]

Start a Ralph loop in your current session.

**Usage:**
```
/ralph-loop "Refactor the cache layer" --max-iterations 20
/ralph-loop "Add tests" --completion-promise "TESTS COMPLETE"
```

**Options:**
- `--max-iterations <n>` - Max iterations before auto-stop
- `--completion-promise <text>` - Promise phrase to signal completion

**How it works:**
1. Creates `.claude/.ralph-loop.local.md` state file
2. You work on the task
3. When you try to exit, stop hook intercepts
4. Same prompt fed back
5. You see your previous work
6. Continues until promise detected or max iterations

---

### /cancel-ralph

Cancel an active Ralph loop (removes the loop state file).

**Usage:**
```
/cancel-ralph
```

**How it works:**
- Checks for active loop state file
- Removes `.claude/.ralph-loop.local.md`
- Reports cancellation with iteration count

---

## Key Concepts

### Completion Promises

To signal completion, Claude must output a `<promise>` tag:

```
<promise>TASK COMPLETE</promise>
```

The stop hook looks for this specific tag. Without it (or `--max-iterations`), Ralph runs infinitely.

### Self-Reference Mechanism

The "loop" doesn't mean Claude talks to itself. It means:
- Same prompt repeated
- Claude's work persists in files
- Each iteration sees previous attempts
- Builds incrementally toward goal

## Example

### Interactive Bug Fix

```
/ralph-loop "Fix the token refresh logic in auth.ts. Output <promise>FIXED</promise> when all tests pass." --completion-promise "FIXED" --max-iterations 10
```

You'll see Ralph:
- Attempt fixes
- Run tests
- See failures
- Iterate on solution
- In your current session

## When to Use Ralph

**Good for:**
- Well-defined tasks with clear success criteria
- Tasks requiring iteration and refinement
- Iterative development with self-correction
- Greenfield projects

**Not good for:**
- Tasks requiring human judgment or design decisions
- One-shot operations
- Tasks with unclear success criteria
- Debugging production issues (use targeted debugging instead)

## Learn More

- Original technique: https://ghuntley.com/ralph/
- Ralph Orchestrator: https://github.com/mikeyobrien/ralph-orchestrator
